note: Per-file RECORDED MINIMUMS: the lowest v8 LINE coverage (`bun run coverage`) and the lowest StrykerJS mutation score (`bun run mutate`) each source file is allowed to report. Both are measured-now values ROUNDED DOWN to a tenth, so timing flap cannot fail a run; raising a recorded minimum rides the commit that earns it. MUTATION re-seeded 2026-08-25 from a CLEARED-CACHE `bun run mutate:full` (3,767 mutants, 25m37s, 92.78% overall) at the normalization campaign's close-out; coverage from a `bun run coverage` run of the same tree. Read the two-sided move that re-seeding produced, because it is the reason the brief asked for a cleared cache: two files ROSE (lines/list-reader.ts 94.6 -> 94.9, print/serialize-inline.ts 96.1 -> 96.5) and six FELL (parse/attrlist.ts 100 -> 98.6, parse/inline/inline-node-builder.ts 87.3 -> 86.9, parse/lines/reader.ts 94.8 -> 94.2, print/blocks.ts 90.6 -> 90.3, print/inline.ts 92.7 -> 92.0, print/list.ts 96.5 -> 96.1). The falls are not a regression in the code: every number they replace came from an INCREMENTAL run that reused a stale cache, and two of the six covered functions that no cleared-cache run had ever measured (attrlistFields and closingQuote, added after the previous seeding). Two of the six were answered with TESTS before the minimum moved (attrlist.ts, and lines/reader.ts's restored tailSafe inheritance); the survivors that remain on those two are classified below as equivalent, with the document counts that establish it. Timing flap is wider than a tenth on the biggest files (inline-node-builder measured 87.3 and 86.9 on two identical-tree runs), so treat a sub-half-point fall on a file with hundreds of mutants as flap to re-measure, not as a regression to bisect. A minimum of 0 means the file has nothing to measure — see the exceptions for the three files Stryker writes no row for at all. HONEST BOUND on `exceptions`: it is the AUDITED set, not every survivor. It holds the two files audited mutant by mutant in W2's recovery, the type-forced and total-fallback arms, the plugin's registration surface, the three files with no mutants, and the three equivalent mutants this close-out proved by differential. The rest of the gap between a recorded minimum and 100% is recorded by the number itself and is a candidate for the next audit. See docs/simplicity-metrics.md, the Recorded minimums section.

exceptions.reason: the AST is interface declarations and nothing else, so there is no expression to mutate; a minimum of 0 here says 'nothing to measure', which is why an unmeasured file with a zero minimum is not an error

exceptions.reason: declarations only, as src/ast.ts

exceptions.what: ArrayDeclaration at index.ts:7 — `languages: [language]` emptied
exceptions.reason: same missing test as src/language.ts: nothing asserts the assembled Plugin object's shape

exceptions.what: all 10 mutants (the SupportLanguage descriptor: name, parsers, extensions, vscodeLanguageIds)
exceptions.reason: a test asserting the descriptor's fields would kill every one of them, and it is not a tautology: which extensions the plugin claims and which parser name it binds ARE the plugin's contract with Prettier. Nothing asserts them today; the identity suite loads the plugin from dist/ and never reads the descriptor

exceptions.what: attrlist.ts:130 `index < raw.length` -> `index <= raw.length` in closingQuote
exceptions.reason: EQUIVALENT. The extra iteration reads `raw[raw.length]`, which is `undefined` and matches neither the escape nor the quote, so the loop still falls through to `return undefined`. Its seven siblings in this file were survivors too until this commit; five new rows in tests/parser/attrlist.test.ts kill them. The one the rows could not have killed is this one

exceptions.what: the `Total fallback:` one-character step (tokenize.ts:54-58) — 7 mutants (6 NoCoverage plus the guard at :54 itself) and the uncovered lines behind the 85.7% coverage minimum
exceptions.reason: unreachable while InlineChar is last in the rule table: it matches any character but a newline, and a newline is matched by InlineNewline. TRIGGER — a rule table where some character matches no rule; the day a rule is removed or narrowed, this arm becomes reachable and gets a test. Kept as a step rather than a throw so the tokenizer stays total whatever the table says

exceptions.what: mutation minimum 0 — Stryker writes no row for this file
exceptions.reason: the inline token-kind names, declared as a const table; no expression to mutate

exceptions.what: the LEFT disjunct of `tailSafe: extent.close !== undefined || this.tailSafe` (reader.ts:850) — 3 mutants: -> `true`, -> `false`, and `!==` -> `===`
exceptions.reason: EQUIVALENT, measured rather than assumed: all three produce byte-identical output over 66,429 documents (a depth-5 product over `----`, `====`, `--`, `****`, `* a`, `** b`, `+`, blank and `para`) and over all 111,121 list-shape sweep documents. Whenever a block CLOSED, the reader's own `tailSafe` is already true, so the left disjunct never decides. The RIGHT disjunct is live and pinned in tests/format/trailing-continuation.test.ts (a trailing `+` at the end of an unclosed `====` or `--` block comes back), which is what took this file from 93.6 to 94.2

exceptions.what: locStart and locEnd bodies (parser.ts:29, :39) — NoCoverage, and the two uncovered lines behind the 50% coverage minimum
exceptions.reason: Prettier calls these only for --range formatting and cursor tracking; the suite formats whole documents. A unit test calling locStart/locEnd on a parsed node would cover and kill both. They are also the reason positions are in the parity comparison at all

exceptions.what: list.ts:141 `lastItem !== undefined` -> `true`
exceptions.reason: Leaves `tailSwallowsMarker(lastItem, block)` reached with `lastItem === undefined` only for a list node with ZERO children, which the reader cannot build — a list exists because an item made it

exceptions.what: list.ts:349 `gap.includes("+")` -> `gap.includes("")`
exceptions.reason:
The blank-run sweep class. The arm fires only when a nested list SHARES its parent's marker, and probing the reader for that shape shows it always arrives with an empty gap — a blank or a `+` in front of a same-marker line reads back as a SIBLING boundary (`* a

  lit
[[anc]]
+
* a
` gives two items). With `gap === []` both spellings return `[]`. TRIGGER — the render-divergent sweep members are the distinguishing shapes; a byte+idempotence pin already guards the drop branch

exceptions.what: list.ts:351 `index > 0` -> `index >= 0`
exceptions.reason: Same as the arm above; `index` comes from `node.blocks.keys()` and is never negative

exceptions.what: list.ts:351 `index > 0` -> `true`
exceptions.reason: Redundant with the third conjunct: at `index === 0`, `slurpReaches(blocks, 0)` scans `blocks.slice(0, 0)` — empty — and returns false, so the condition is false either way

exceptions.what: list.ts:401 `blankRun = false` -> `blankRun = true` in gapParts's `+` arm
exceptions.reason: EQUIVALENT. The only read of `blankRun` is `!livePlus && blankRun` (list.ts:405), the `+` arm sets `livePlus` in the line above, and nothing clears it — so after a `+` the value can never be read again. Zero byte differences over all 111,121 list-shape sweep documents

exceptions.what: list.ts:84 `block.type === "delimitedBlock"` -> `true`
exceptions.reason: Leaves `block.form === "indented"`. No other block node can carry that form: `delimitedBlock` is the only `BlockNode` with `form: … | "indented"` (`admonition`'s form is `"paragraph"` or a parent-block variant; `link`/`xref` forms are inline). The AST forbids the difference

exceptions.what: the default arm of the node dispatch (printer.ts:141-143) — 3 NoCoverage mutants
exceptions.reason: an EQUIVALENT arm forced by the type system: Prettier's AstPath is invariant, so the printer's node union must admit the inline nodes a paragraph's children array is typed with. Every block that owns inline content builds its atoms itself, so no path reaches this arm; deleting it is a type error

exceptions.what: the empty-document arm (printer.ts:53 conditional, :56 the empty string) — 3 mutants
exceptions.reason: formatting an empty document is reachable — parse("") — and nothing formats one. A fixture for the empty document would kill all three

exceptions.what: reflow.ts:227 `/\s+/v` -> `/\s/v` in splitWords
exceptions.reason: The only difference between the two splits is the empty strings a single-character split emits between adjacent whitespace, and `.filter((word) => word.length > 0)` erases exactly those. The two produce the same array for every input

exceptions.what: reflow.ts:350 `last < 0` -> `false` in escapeDanglingPlus
exceptions.reason: Dead by the caller contract: `endNodeAtoms` is the only caller and has already returned when `last < 0`, so the guard re-checks a state it can never be in. Killing it needs a direct call with an empty atom list — a test-only construction of unreachable state

exceptions.what: reflow.ts:434 `let glueNext = false` -> `true` in wordsToAtoms
exceptions.reason: The initializer is read only on the first iteration, and there `fuseBackwards = index > 0 && (glueNext || …)` short-circuits on `index > 0` before `glueNext` is looked at. Every later read sees the value the previous iteration assigned

exceptions.what: narrow()'s guard and message (unreachable.ts:46-48), 6 mutants and the uncovered third of the file
exceptions.reason: narrow() is @internal, exported for the test helpers, and its throw fires only when two places that agree have drifted apart. Killing the mutants means constructing the impossible state on purpose — a test-only construction of unreachable state, which is the thing the defense inventory exists to shrink, not to pin
